Testimony ofRepresentative Morgan Rielly introducing
LD 1576, An Act to Extend a One-year Lobbying Prohibition to Partisan and
Nonpartisan Staff of the Legislature
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Aflairs

Good afternoon, Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. I am Morgan Rielly, and I represent House District 127, which includes part of Westbrook. Thank you for the opportunity to
introduce LD 1576, An Act to Extend a One-year Lobbying Prohibition to Partisan and
Nonpartisan Staff of the Legislature for your consideration.

This bill is straightforward. It addresses what I feel is a gap in our laws regarding our one-year lobbying prohibition by extending it to partisan and nonpartisan staff in the Legislature.

Legislative Staff should be held to the same lobbying standards as legislators and executive branch employees. I want to be clear -- this bill isn't about any particular Staff. This is about addressing the gap that has been created with the current exemption. I don't think it is appropriate for partisan and nonpartisan staff to have the ability to work in the State House on a Friday and then lobby their former committees or legislators on a Monday.

Leaving during the session or in between sessions to lobby undermines trust, not just with legislators, but with the broader public. It also creates an unfair advantage for the lobby, with staff being privy to caucus or committee information and having close connections with current
legislators. To avoid this, we should extend the same one-year lobbying ban to the staff of the
Legislature.
Thank you -very much for your time and consideration. I'm happy to answer any questions or
provide any further information for the work session.

Testimony --~ Lyda Libby Prepared for Maine State Legislature -- 05/05/2025 Cannabis Policy Session
Good morning, members of the committee. My name is Lyda Libby and I am a
resident of Wiscasset. I'm a longtime medical cannabis patient, a creative cannabis
artist, and a budtender here in Maine.
My message is simple: Free the plant.
Cannabis is medicine. Cannabis is agriculture. It's a medicinal plant--and it deserves the same respect as any other healing herb growing in our gardens.
In my work, I've had the honor of helping patients through some of the most
vulnerable moments of their lives- supporting them through chronic pain, emotional distress, and even end-of-life care. Cannabis gave them comfort, relief, and moments of peace.
Patients shouldn't be burdened with arbitrary THC caps that ignore their individual
needs. They shouldn't face delays because caregivers are forced to navigate l\/IETRC, or comply with costly testing and packaging mandates that add expense
without adding value. We need policies that free the plant from systems designed
for corporate compliance. Yes, safe and affordable medicine is the goal----but
overregulation is not how we protect patients.
We protect them by building community, not by creating barriers. They rely on
locally grown, caregiver-crafted medicine----grown with love, knowledge, and intention. They also need access, education, and connection. Events give patients a chance to connect, ask questions, and feel seen. Cannabis has always been more than commerce. It's culture, history, and resilience.
I was born here in Maine, and I've grown here too. This is where I'm learning how
to live with intention--hoW to speak up, stay grounded, and move with purpose.
Maine has that same potential. We don't have to follow other states. We can grow
something uniquely our own. Our motto is Dirigo----I lead. Let's live up to it.
Let's build a model that's thoughtful, sustainable, and deeply human----one that reflects not just what the cannabis industry could be, but what it should be: compassionate, community-driven, and rooted in care.

I support LD 1672, 1820, 1840, and l897----bills that protect caregivers, promote
sun-grown cultivation, expand access to events, and respect the plant's natural place in our communities. Outdoor cultivation is not only traditional, it's
environmentally responsible. I also support LD 1488, 1567, and 1620, which bring
transparency and balance, and prohibit the use of ionizing radiation on cannabis
products.
I strongly oppose LD 104 and LD 1847, which would impose l\/IETRC tracking, along with mandated testing, THC caps, and taxes that many patients simply
cannot afford. That's not regulation--it's restriction. And it threatens the
foundation of what makes this program work.
A program that was built by the people. By hands in the soil and hearts in the work.
The caregivers, patients, small growers, herbalists, educators--we are the heart of
it. And we're simply asking for the space to keep doing what we've done for years:
grow clean medicine, support our neighbors, and serve with integrity.
I. ask you not just to protect this program, but to nurture it. To believe in what's already working. To listen to the people living this every day-----and to help us build a future where the plant, the people, and the purpose don't just survive----but thrive.
Thank you for your time, your attention, and your openness.
Please--free the plant.
